key_terms.meaning: Processing that amplifies, filters, linearises and isolates a sensor output before digitisation.
Device that converts a physical quantity into an electrical signal, e.g. a thermocouple gives volts per °C.
Switch that connects one of many sensor channels to a single ADC input in a chosen order.
Circuit that freezes the analogue input while the ADC converts it, so the value does not change mid-conversion.
ADC that tests bits from MSB to LSB, taking n clock steps for an n-bit result.
Oversampling ADC that trades high sample rate for high resolution using noise shaping and digital filtering.
Transmission standard where 4 mA marks zero and 20 mA full scale; current stays the same along a series loop.
Unwanted path formed when two grounded points sit at different potentials, causing current and noise in a signal cable.
Actuator that converts compressed air pressure into force using a cylinder or diaphragm.
Actuator that converts pressurised oil into large force using a cylinder, motor or rotary vane.
Coil that pulls a magnetic plunger through a short stroke when current flows.
Electrically operated switch whose coil moves contacts to open or close a separate circuit.
Motor that rotates in fixed steps when pulses arrive; step angle θ = 360°/N for N steps per revolution.
Motor with position or speed feedback that corrects error until output follows the command.
Actuator that strains when voltage is applied; strain is small but fast and forceful, with little heat.
Metal that changes shape on heating above a transition temperature and can return on cooling.
Four-arm resistive bridge balanced when R1/R2 = R3/R4, giving zero detector voltage.
AC bridge that measures unknown inductance by balancing it against a known capacitance and resistance.
Amplifier that passes signal while blocking direct electrical connection, breaking ground loops and protecting circuits.
Oscilloscope that samples, digitises and stores a waveform so one-time events can be displayed.

takeaways: Signal conditioning must match the sensor output range and impedance to the ADC input range and must reject noise before conversion.
A data acquisition system is only as good as its weakest link: resolution, sampling rate, settling time and channel order all matter.
Current loops and differential transmission protect small signals over long distances.
Pneumatic actuators suit clean, spark-free, moderate-force work; hydraulic actuators suit high force.
Solenoids and relays give on/off motion; motors give continuous motion.
Stepper motors are simple open-loop positioners; servo motors use feedback for accuracy under load.
Micro actuators are chosen for small size and speed, not for large force.
Bridges measure unknown R, L or C by null balance, and display instruments trade bandwidth against accuracy.
bank_note: Long answers are expected to carry block diagrams, bridge balance conditions, ADC and actuator comparisons, and clear calculations with units, not just definitions.

bank.q: Draw the block diagram of a data acquisition system and explain the job of each block.
outline: Transducer and signal conditioner
Multiplexer and sample-and-hold
ADC and processor or controller
Store, display or bus interface

bank.q: Define signal conditioning. List and explain amplification, filtering, linearisation and isolation.
outline: Definition and need near the sensor
Amplification for small signals
Filtering to remove noise and aliasing
Linearisation and electrical isolation

bank.q: Compare a stepper motor and a servo motor on motion, feedback, cost and load behaviour.
outline: Stepper moves in fixed steps, often open-loop
Servo uses encoder or resolver feedback
Servo corrects error under load
Cost and complexity comparison

bank.q: A thermocouple gives 8 mV at 200 °C and 0 mV at 0 °C. Design a signal conditioner to give 0–5 V; find gain and explain the filter and isolation you add.
outline: Gain = 5 V / 8 mV = 625
Use instrumentation or differential amplifier
Add low-pass filter for noise
Add isolation to break ground loops

bank.q: An 8-bit ADC has reference 5 V. Find resolution and output code for 2.0 V; state one error source.
outline: Resolution = 5/255 ≈ 19.6 mV
Quantisation error of ±½ LSB
Reference drift or missing sample-and-hold

bank.q: A 4–20 mA transmitter reads 12 mA. Find the percentage of full scale and the voltage across a 250 Ω receiver resistor.
outline: Voltage V = I × R = 12 mA × 250 Ω = 3 V
4 mA is live zero, not 0 % current
Loop supply must exceed total voltage drop

bank.q: A hydraulic cylinder has piston area 0.005 m² and oil pressure 10 MPa. Find force; choose it over a pneumatic cylinder for a press and justify.
outline: Force F = p × A = 10 MPa × 0.005 m² = 50 kN
Hydraulic oil gives high force in small size
Pneumatic air is compressible and spark-free
Press needs stiffness and force, so hydraulic suits

bank.q: A stepper motor has 200 steps/rev and drives a 5 mm pitch lead screw. Find pulses to move 20 mm; state whether feedback is needed.
outline: 20 mm / 5 mm = 4 revolutions
Open-loop works if load never exceeds torque
Feedback needed if steps may be lost

bank.q: A signal cable runs 80 m beside a motor drive. Choose voltage or current transmission, explain shielding and grounding, and calculate loop voltage at 20 mA through 100 Ω.
outline: Prefer 4–20 mA current loop for long runs
Use twisted pair with shield grounded at one end
Avoid ground loops and use differential input

bank.q: Compare flash, SAR and sigma-delta ADCs on speed, resolution, cost and noise; select one for audio and one for a slow temperature logger.
outline: Flash: fastest, low resolution, many comparators
SAR: medium speed, good resolution, common choice
Sigma-delta: slow to medium, high resolution, filters noise
Audio suits sigma-delta; temperature logger suits sigma-delta or SAR

bank.q: A low-level sensor shows 50 Hz hum and a slowly drifting offset. Analyse likely causes and propose differential amplifier, filtering and isolation.
outline: Hum from mains pickup or ground loop
Drift from temperature, bias current or electrode offset
Differential amplifier rejects common-mode voltage
Low-pass or notch filter and isolation amplifier reduce hum

bank.q: Evaluate electrostatic, piezoelectric and shape-memory micro actuators for a MEMS RF switch; include pull-in, hysteresis, force and speed.
outline: Electrostatic: fast, low force, pull-in instability
Piezoelectric: fast, higher force, small strain
SMA: large motion, slow, hysteresis and heat
RF switch needs low loss, repeatability and reasonable voltage

bank.q: Explain how a DSO captures a single fast pulse; compare with a CRO using bandwidth, sampling rate, memory and triggering.
outline: DSO samples and stores before display
Sampling rate must exceed signal bandwidth
Trigger and memory capture one-time events
CRO shows live trace but cannot store easily

bank.q: A Kelvin bridge and a Wheatstone bridge are offered for 0.001 Ω measurement. Evaluate lead resistance, sensitivity and practical use.
outline: Wheatstone lead resistance adds error at low R
Kelvin bridge uses four-terminal connection
Kelvin separates current and voltage leads
Choose Kelvin for low resistance, Wheatstone for ordinary R

glossary.def: The processing of a sensor signal to make it suitable for transmission or digitisation.
A device that changes a physical quantity into an electrical output.
Analogue-to-digital converter; it turns a continuous voltage into a digital code.
The smallest input change an ADC or display can show, often one least significant bit.
The number of samples taken per second, measured in samples per second or hertz.
A low-pass filter placed before an ADC to remove frequencies above half the sampling rate.
Correction that makes a non-linear sensor output proportional to the measured quantity.
Separation that lets signal pass but blocks direct current paths between circuits.
Components that divert or clamp high-voltage transients before they damage a circuit.
Supervisory control and data acquisition; a distributed system for monitoring and controlling plant.
A current transmission standard with 4 mA at zero and 20 mA at full scale.
Two insulated wires twisted together so picked-up noise tends to cancel.
A tube and piston that produce linear force from compressed air.
A valve that sets the direction, pressure or flow of oil in a hydraulic circuit.
A valve opened or closed by a solenoid coil.
The moving and fixed metal pieces that open or close a relay circuit.
Voltage induced by a changing magnetic field when a coil current is switched off.
The fixed angle a stepper motor turns for one pulse, equal to 360° divided by steps per revolution.
A sensor signal that reports actual position or speed so the controller can correct error.
The voltage at which electrostatic force overcomes spring force and a micro plate snaps down.
A four-arm resistance bridge used to find an unknown resistance by null balance.
A four-terminal bridge that measures very low resistance without lead resistance error.
An AC bridge used to measure capacitance and loss angle of a capacitor.
Digital storage oscilloscope; it samples and stores waveforms for display and analysis.
